title: Agents
text: pressfreedom R package bundling Shiny dashboard exploring Reporters Without Borders (RSF) Press Freedom Index. dashboard three views: Map — choropleth world, colored score/rank/dimension chosen year; low-friction entry point data. Trends — multi-country line charts (Score) bump charts (Rank) 2002–2025. Country — single country’s profile: horizontal Rank/Score stat table, score-band/rank-tier count bar charts, two combined trend charts (Score + dimensions, Rank + dimension ranks) sharing one deduplicated legend. Clicking country Map point Trends chart jumps Country profile (see “Shared navigation” ).

text: app uses fully modular design (inst/app/), built bslib::page_navbar() single id = "view" navset switching three nav_panel()s wired app.R: Map, Trends, Country. page_navbar()’s installed version (0.11.0) per-nav_panel() sidebar = argument — one page-level sidebar =, shared across panels — per-view sidebar content achieved navset_hidden(id = "sidebar_view") inside single sidebar, kept sync visible navbar tabs via nav_select("sidebar_view", input$view) observer server. mod_map — choropleth (plotly::plot_geo()) colored Score, Rank, 2022+ dimension. Year choices react zone metric (dimensions restrict 2022+, score 2013+). Score-like metrics use RSF’s real 5-class band classification; Rank uses percentile tiers — exposed independent checkboxGroupInput toggles grey (remove) unchecked bands. See “Map score/rank bands” . mod_chart (Trends) — renders plotly card, reused two contexts: standalone Trends view (multi-country, show_nav = TRUE) embedded Country view compact mode single country (show_nav = FALSE). Score → scatter line chart; Rank → ggbump bump chart converted via ggplotly(). interactive behavior (hover-dimming click--navigate) handled client-side via JavaScript (onRender) — see “Client-side JavaScript approach chart interactivity” . mod_country — flag/name header; overview card horizontal Rank/Score stat table (current/best/worst/mean--median/biggest advance/biggest decline) plus two small band/tier count bar charts (score bands via rsf_band(), rank tiers via rank_tier() per-year max_rank, reused mod_map.R); trend row two bespoke combined charts — Score (+ 5 context dimensions, 2022–2025) Rank (+ 5 dimension-rank columns, rank_pol etc.) — merged via plotly::subplot() one deduplicated, floating legend (dimension traces share legendgroup across panels; score panel’s copy sets showlegend = TRUE). hand-built plot_ly()/ggplot2+ggbump calls local mod_country.R, reuse mod_chart.R — see “Dimension data (2022+): per-view treatment” . mod_inputs (Trends sidebar) — selectInputs variable (Score/Rank — dimensions intentionally excluded, see ) country (multiple selection). helpers.R — df_chart() filters/prepares data; card_title() builds dynamic card header. flags.R — maps rwb_standardized$iso (alpha-3) flagon’s alpha-2 flag codes; see “Flags (flagon)” . app.R wires modules loads data via pressfreedom.data::rwb_standardized. module files use explicit package namespacing (e.g., shiny::, dplyr::) additional library() calls needed inside modules, except library(ggplot2) app.R (required ggplotly() resolves variables name search path). Score scale-transition artifact (2013): RSF changed scoring methodology 2013. score exists back 2002, pre-2013 2013+ values sit two incompatible scales — mixing aggregate (mean/median, band counts, min/max) understates overstates real standing. score_evolution (score - score_n_1) additionally compares two scales directly single transition year, producing artifacts large +5,763 aren’t real year--year changes. rank_evolution unaffected (rank -year relative ordering years, regardless underlying score scale). Resolution: mod_country.R’s score stat block (stat_table) score-band bar chart (score_band_data) filter year_n >= 2013 computing anything, score_evolution additionally set NA year_n == 2013 (scoped locally — underlying rwb_standardized$score_evolution column untouched) since even first comparable year’s evolution diff incompatible prior value. use score score_evolution elsewhere multi-year aggregate, apply year_n >= 2013 filter (2013 score_evolution exclusion, using evolution) surface artifact.

what: Nonce collision pitfall: identical values silently skip reactiveVal observers
title: Agents
text: Map Trends modules return list(country = ..., nonce = ...) app-level selected_country reactiveVal. nonce critical — reactiveVal silently skips calling observers assigned identical() value current one. fix (module-local integer counters): module used click_nonce <- 0 incremented 1 click. Clicking country map (nonce = 1) chart (nonce = 1) produced identical() values: silently broke navigation first chart click session (second clicks increment chart nonce beyond 1). Fix: Use .numeric(proc.time()[["elapsed"]]) instead integer counters. elapsed seconds since R process startup globally unique across modules re-executions: Apply pattern new module feeds selected_country reactiveVal needs distinguish repeated values.
code: # map click selected_country(list(country = "Algeria", nonce = 1))  # chart click on same country selected_country(list(country = "Algeria", nonce = 1))  # identical(), observer skipped # map click selected_country(list(country = "Algeria", nonce = 12345.678))  # chart click on same country selected_country(list(country = "Algeria", nonce = 12345.789))  # not identical(), observer fires

what: Client-side JavaScript approach for chart interactivity
title: Agents
text: interactive behavior Trends chart (click--navigate hover-dimming) now handled entirely client-side via JavaScript (htmlwidgets::onRender), rather R-side plotly event handlers plotlyProxy restyle commands. : Early attempts used R-side plotlyProxy() restyle hover dim non-hovered traces. first hover (client-side plotly traces fully initialized), triggered coerceTraceIndices error plotly’s JavaScript. error ran Shiny message batch navigation nav_select() triggered simultaneous click, error aborted entire message batch, silently swallowing navigation command. Current implementation: mod_chart.R’s renderPlotly, onRender callback installs three event listeners: Click--navigate: Extracts country name directly clicked trace (el.data[curveNumber].name, set plot_ly(color=) ggplot aes(color=)), calls Shiny.setInputValue() priority = 'event' ensure every click fires. Hover-dimming: Extracts hovered curveNumber, loops traces, sets opacities 1 hovered trace 0.15 others via Plotly.restyle() — instant, server round-trip. Unhover: Restores traces full opacity. design eliminates timing issue makes hover-dimming snappier. revert plotlyProxy restyle observeEvent(event_data("plotly_hover", ...)) — coerceTraceIndices error return.

what: Trends tooltip content and the bump chart’s legend dedup
title: Agents
text: Trends chart types show 3-line hover tooltip — flag emoji + country name, Year: <n>, Score:/Rank: <value> — built explicit hover_text column (flag_emoji(iso) + country_en + year_n + metric value) rather relying plotly’s default x/y/name hover. score branch native plot_ly(), direct: text = ~hover_text, hoverinfo = "text". rank branch goes ggplot2 + ggbump::geom_bump() + ggplotly(), constrained: hover_text mapped via ggplot2::aes(text = hover_text) geom_point() (real yearly data points), geom_bump() (stat-transformed, interpolated curve whose intermediate rows aren’t real year/rank pairs — mapping text show misleading values). ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text") uses mapping. geom_bump()’s line layer text aes, ggplotly() otherwise show empty/NA hover box hovering connecting curve two yearly points. Fixed identifying line-mode traces post-hoc disabling hover entirely: plotly::style(p_final, hoverinfo = "none", traces = line_traces) line_traces <- (vapply(p_final$x$data, function(tr) identical(tr$mode, "lines"), logical(1))). Fix: decouple legend real traces entirely. plotly::style(p_final, showlegend = FALSE, traces = seq_along(p_final$x$data)) hides legend every real trace, one proxy add_trace() per country supplies single "lines+markers" swatch sized match score chart (marker = list(size = 20), line = list(width = 4)). Proxy trace point placement — use numeric(0) NA: empty vector (x = numeric(0), y = numeric(0)) looks like safest way make proxy trace invisible, plotly::plotly_build() found (empirically) silently corrupt — trace’s x/y end literal strings "x"/"y" instead numeric data, legend entry never renders. scalar NA point opposite problem: plot_ly()’s trace-building drops , along name/legendgroup metadata, since looks like “data mapped”. fix works: real, far---range scalar point (x = -1e6, y = -1e6). ggplotly() already fixes chart’s axis ranges explicitly (autorange = FALSE axes, confirmed via p_final$x$layout), sentinel point simply clipped -canvas fixed range can’t perturb visible plot trigger autorange. hover-dimming fix (grouping trace name/country rather curveNumber, country’s “lines” “markers” sub-traces dim together) lives shared onRender script — see “Client-side JavaScript approach chart interactivity” . add third color-mapped layer chart, re-verify whole proxy-trace setup — new real trace changes trace ggplotly() otherwise pick showlegend = TRUE, though explicit style(showlegend = FALSE, ...) real traces absorb automatically. Legend entry order sorted match curves’ vertical position final year: ascending rank (best rank first, since scale_y_reverse() puts “best” top) — rank-axis mirror score branch’s descending--value sort, already place change. bump chart’s start/end geom_text(label = iso) layers (ISO codes ends curve) removed legend took identifying curve country.

what: “Deselect all” clobbering a just-restored partial selection on metric switch
title: Agents
text: Symptom (reported, reproduced, fixed): customize Score partial selection (e.g. “Good”), switch Rank customize (e.g. “Top 2.5%”), switch back Score — just-restored partial selection got silently overwritten back “everything checked” (countries colored). Confusingly, appeared asymmetric: sometimes Score revisit failed Rank revisit succeeded, sometimes reverse — depending metric user recently used “Deselect ” checkbox switching away . Root cause: “Deselect ” checkbox (input$deselect_all) stateful toggle — checking clears every band, unchecking restores full set — implemented via observeEvent(input$deselect_all, ...) unconditionally calling updateCheckboxGroupInput(..., selected = (checked) character(0) else levels_). Separately, code needs keep toggle’s displayed value honest side effect actions (e.g. syncing unchecked user manually re-checks one band using “Deselect ”, resetting metric-change observer restores saved non-empty selection). side effects work calling shiny::updateCheckboxInput(session, "deselect_all", value = ...). updateCheckboxInput() changing value indistinguishable, inside input$deselect_all observer, genuine user click — programmatic “sync display unchecked” call immediately retrigger observer’s full-reset logic, overwriting selection triggered sync (e.g. metric-change observer’s just-applied restore). Fix: deselect_all_tracked reactiveVal records value module recently assigned input$deselect_all (whether via genuine user click programmatic sync). Every programmatic updateCheckboxInput(session, "deselect_all", value = X) call preceded deselect_all_tracked(X). observeEvent(input$deselect_all, ...) handler opens (identical(input$deselect_all, deselect_all_tracked())) return(invisible(NULL)) — update’s echo arrives client, ’s recognised module’s destructive reset skipped; value differs deselect_all_tracked() (real, new user click) runs reset logic. input$bands observer also gained matching sync block (see comment ) fix closely-related “Deselect stays checked user manually re-checks band” bug — guard, reactiveVal. remove deselect_all_tracked “unwrap” unnecessary indirection — every one do_reset_map(), metric-change observer, input$bands sync block relies make updateCheckboxInput() calls silent -ops input$deselect_all observer’s point view.

text: map’s zoom pan state persist user changes sidebar controls (Metric, Year, Zone, band/tier checkboxes) switches tabs away back. achieved via plotly.js’s uirevision layout attribute: uirevision remains constant across figure redraws (Shiny triggers every control change), plotly.js preserves user-driven view state (zoom, pan, geo projection). uirevision changes, view resets layout’s default. mapServer(), reactiveVal named map_view_id holds unique token (via proc.time()[["elapsed"]]) passed plotly::layout(..., uirevision = map_view_id()) every render. normal circumstances — metric switch, band toggle, year/zone change — map_view_id() never changes, zoom/pan sticks. do_reset_map() (called sidebar’s “Clear” button app’s “Reset ” button) bumps value, triggering plotly.js drop back default geo view. uirevision alone sufficient — also requires transition layout. plotly R package’s Shiny htmlwidget binding (renderValue() JS) calls Plotly.react() — call actually honors uirevision — layout$transition truthy. Without , every renderPlotly() re-run instead Plotly.purge() followed Plotly.newPlot(), full teardown/rebuild discards preserved zoom/pan state regardless whether uirevision matched. map’s plotly::layout() call therefore also sets transition = list(duration = 0) (zero duration ’s visible animation, just route react() code path). verified empirically: uirevision alone, zoom/pan still reset every control change; switching tabs back “worked” path never re-executes renderPlotly() , never exercised purge/newPlot bug. Important: mutate map_view_id() elsewhere module, remove either uirevision transition entries plotly::layout() call — required together. Future changes band/tier logic control-change reactive chain affect mechanism. route band/tier color changes plotlyProxy() restyle calls “lighter-weight” alternative full renderPlotly() re-render. tried (reading checked_bands() separate observeEvent() restyled trace colors index, output$map ignored checkbox state) theory skipping full re-render help preserve zoom/pan. ’s unnecessary now uirevision/transition already make full re-renders preserve zoom/pan, actively broke color rendering: proxy restyle’s trace-index bookkeeping (built re-walking levels_/map_data() skipping empty bands) can race concurrent full re-render triggered reactive flush (e.g. do_reset_map() changing metric/zone/year band selection together), targeting stale mismatched trace indices leaving map uncolored — intermittently “Clear”, reliably enough look “random”. output$map’s renderPlotly() reads checked_bands() directly rebuilds traces every relevant change instead; correct, current design — keep way.

title: Launch the Press Freedom Dashboard — run_app
code: if (interactive()) {   # Launch with defaults   run_app()    # Launch without opening a browser automatically, e.g. inside an   # IDE's viewer pane or a remote session   run_app(launch.browser = FALSE)    # Pin a specific port, e.g. to satisfy a firewall rule   run_app(port = 8080) }
